tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic two-event root recovery boundary with event1 and event2 already durable exactly once, root processing represented completely by one atomic repository-visible processed=false->processed=true state transition, and acknowledgment unavailable after attempting that transition.

resume_actions: processed=false -> perform the single durable root-processing state transition to processed=true

invariants_verified: event1 and event2 remain exactly once in both allowed atomic post-crash states
resume never re-appends either durable event
both allowed states converge to processed=true
a state already processed=true never performs a second root-processing state transition
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to the exact state machine above, including the assumption that root processing has no hidden non-idempotent effect outside the atomic repository-visible processed state. It does not establish safety for external side effects, torn/corrupt writes, concurrent writers, identity collisions, nested frames, other event counts, arbitrary Unicode, hostile-size behavior, or Phase-1 closure.
scientific_interpretation: For this recurrence-sensitive checkpoint boundary, recovery can treat lost acknowledgment as an observation problem rather than a retry problem: reconstruct durable event identity membership and the atomic processed state, then execute only the missing state transition. This is analogous to state-estimation from persistent sufficient statistics: the durable state is sufficient for choosing the next transition within the tested scope.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one adjacent child-root-to-parent completion-record append acknowledgment ambiguity. Hold child root processed=true with event1/event2 durable; parent completion identity is repository-observable as either absent or present exactly once after an unacknowledged append attempt. Verify resume appends only when absent and never duplicates when present.
